title: Review: relay_queue round-6 fixes
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — The break-on-entry-error pattern across all three directory scans is a latent bug class that any contributor will copy into future scan loops. The widened .tmp deletion contract is not documented and has no test distinguishing old from new behaviour.
Confidence: 10% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: yevk.2 (broader .tmp deletion may be intentional design decision, not a bug — the dir is operator-controlled). Uncertainty driven by: cannot see git history of round-6 or the PR description to know if widening the .tmp deletion was deliberate. Would raise confidence if: round-6 commit message or PR body explains the intent of the extension() change.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — The relay_queue.rs code itself is idiomatically sound. The Rust-specific issues (missing Debug, non_exhaustive, pub visibility on test helper, leaky Arc<Mutex>) are in supporting types (relay_health.rs, relay_error.rs, config.rs) that fall within the review scope. No unsafe, no gratuitous clones, no iterator anti-patterns in the implementation code.
Rust idiom confidence: 15% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: yevk.14 (structured error fields) — this is a genuine trade-off; the all_variants_classified test shows the author thought carefully about exhaustiveness, and some SMTP clients don't distinguish within 4xx/5xx ranges anyway. Uncertainty driven by: cannot see how callers consume SmtpRelayError outside relay_queue.rs — if all callers only check is_transient()/is_permanent(), the String wrapping is fine.
